$comment: The canonical MCP client table: the one home for per-client config facts.
Everything downstream reads this file, zero drift:
- the Brilliant desktop app and web editor: a table generated from this file
- the npx installer: lib/install.js reads THIS file directly (same package ships it)
desktop.urlEntry = the DESKTOP app's loopback HTTP MCP server (127.0.0.1:3333/mcp); a URL entry.
stdio.entry      = the @brilliant-hq/mcp helper (npx -y @brilliant-hq/mcp); a stdio command entry.
'$URL' in urlEntry is the placeholder the desktop app fills with the live endpoint (via urlKey).
configPath.base is 'home' (~) or 'appData' (Windows %APPDATA%). segments join under it.
'verified' lists the official-doc source URLs each row's syntax was checked against (2026-08).
A note that starts 'DRIFT:' records where a shipped desktop value and the client's current docs differed, and which one this row now holds.

clients.notes: URL entry REQUIRES type:http (a bare url with no type is a hard config error). stdio: no-type => stdio, type:stdio optional. CLI `claude mcp add <name> -- <cmd>` (the -- is required).

No CLI add subcommand. Remote entry uses bare url (no type). Deep link: the `cursor://anysphere.cursor-deeplink/mcp/install?name=<name>&config=<base64(entryJson)>` form is community-widespread but UNVERIFIED against Cursor's official deeplink reference (which documents the host but only prompt/command/rule paths): left null until confirmable.

Container is `servers` (NOT mcpServers). User config is JSONC. Remote REQUIRES type:http. stdio omits type in official examples. CLI `code --add-mcp '<json>'` where json carries a name field. Deep-link scheme `vscode:mcp/install?<urlencoded-json>` is verified; the insiders.vscode.dev redirect form is UNVERIFIED.

clients.restartHint: Restart your Codex session (or the ChatGPT desktop app) to connect.
clients.notes: TOML [mcp_servers.<name>]. Streamable-HTTP uses url = "..." in the same table (no transport flag). stdio uses command/args. The Brilliant desktop app also registers Codex in this section. `codex mcp add <name> -- <cmd>` verified to exist. The ChatGPT desktop app reads the SAME ~/.codex/config.toml mcp_servers table, so this one entry serves both surfaces; never add a second row for it, that would double-write the file.

clients.restartHint: Restart your Gemini CLI session to connect.
clients.notes: httpUrl selects streamable HTTP; a bare url would select SSE (load-bearing distinction). stdio uses command/args. `gemini mcp add <name> -- <cmd>` verified; `-t http <name> <url>` for the remote form.

Uses serverUrl (url/httpUrl explicitly NOT supported). stdio uses command/args. No terminal CLI (in-app /mcp + MCP Store only). DRIFT: shipped config path is ~/.gemini/antigravity/mcp_config.json; 2026-08 official docs say ~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json (global) or .agents/mcp_config.json (workspace). FLIPPED to the documented path (2026-08-16); old installs at ~/.gemini/antigravity/ re-toggle once.

Uses serverUrl (not url) for HTTP. stdio uses command/args. Deep-link `windsurf://windsurf-mcp-registry?serverName=<name>` exists but is REGISTRY-only (marketplace entry), cannot inject a custom local server, so left null.

settings.json is JSONC. context_servers container. stdio is flat command/args (verified). DRIFT: shipped desktop urlEntry is {source:custom,url}; 2026-08 Zed main-branch docs show a bare {url} for remote (source dropped; the nested source:custom form was the OLD stdio shape). FLIPPED to the documented bare {url} (2026-08-16). Windows path %APPDATA%\Zed is unverified (kept as shipped).

clients.restartHint: Restart your OpenCode session to connect.
clients.notes: HTTP (remote): {type:remote,url,enabled} (verified, matches shipped). stdio (local): {type:local,command:[array],enabled}: command is a single array, not command/args; env key is `environment`. `opencode mcp add` CLI exists but exact stdio arg syntax is not documented on the MCP page, so webConnectCommand stays the universal npx one-liner (future: wire the CLI add once syntax is confirmed).

Container is the ONE flat dotted key `amp.mcpServers` (not a nested amp object). Remote entry is a bare {url} (the CLI help says `amp mcp add <name> <url>` is a remote server with auto-detected transport). stdio is command/args. The Amp CLI (0.0.1790251618, 2026-09-24) reads and rewrites a settings.json carrying // comments, so JSONC. `amp mcp add <name> -- <cmd>` verified against the real CLI help. Windows path %USERPROFILE%\.config\amp is inferred from ~ (unverified on a Windows box). Workspace .amp/settings.json is not written (needs per-workspace approval in Amp).

clients.restartHint: Restart your muse session to connect.
clients.notes: Muse Code (Meta, binary `muse`). Verified against the docs bundled in the Muse Code 1.4.6 binary (no public doc URL) and probed on a temp home: the file is ${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/muse/settings.json, the container is camelCase `mcpServers`; the snake `mcp_servers` still loads alone but is LEGACY, and both keys at once fault the whole MCP member (`muse mcp login` says 'MCP configuration is faulted'), so the writer renames a legacy-only `mcp_servers` (legacyContainer). A missing or unsupported top-level schema_version refuses the file ('missing field `schema_version`', 'unsupported settings schema version 99'), so the writer adds `schema_version: 1` when absent (requiredTopLevel) and never rewrites a present one. Entry: transport streamable_http + url + mode optional (Muse docs: always write mode optional, never mode and required together). `muse mcp` has only OAuth login/logout, no add subcommand, so cliAdd is null and the stdio installer does not configure Muse (it would need the same two laws in the JS writer). Windows: Muse documents only $XDG_CONFIG_HOME or $HOME/.config (no %APPDATA% root anywhere in the binary), so the home path holds on every OS (unverified on a Windows box). XDG_CONFIG_HOME is not honoured by the desktop writer.

desktop.unavailableReason: Claude Desktop's config supports only local stdio servers; remote HTTP connections aren't supported yet.

clients.notes: FLIPS from unsupported (desktop URL surface: stdio-only config can't take a remote HTTP URL) to SUPPORTED for the stdio helper: the npx installer CAN configure it; the desktop settings toggle cannot. No CLI add; JSON file only. Config file is macOS/Windows only officially; Linux path (~/Library/Application Support/Claude) is Brilliant's shipped fallback, NOT an official Anthropic path.
